topSignals.title: Ceres Power signs a new, unnamed European (EMEA) SOFC manufacturing licensee — a sixth licensee alongside Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai, Denso and Thermax.
topSignals.text: A privately-owned European energy-technology company (identity withheld, "to be released in due course") has taken a non-exclusive licence to manufacture Ceres' Endura SOFC platform for the EMEA market, with an option to expand to a global licence if exercised by 2035. The partner plans a dedicated facility targeting c. 200 MW/yr — well below Bloom's 2,000 MW/yr Fremont benchmark and Elcogen's 360 MW/yr Tallinn factory, so this does not challenge the manufacturing-capacity register. Initial licence-fee revenue recognition lifts Ceres' contracted FY26 revenue to roughly £60m. This item was missed by this monitor's Nov 19 and Nov 23 Ceres Power dedicated searches (announced Nov 16) and is being logged today on re-discovery. Ceres Power newsroom

topSignals.title: Thirteenth consecutive quiet day on priority stacks — Elcogen now 25 days quiet, Topsoe 92 days.
topSignals.text: Dedicated searches for both priority stacks (English and German), today's Tier 2 rotation round 2 (Ceres Power — see above; Sunfire — no new item) and sweep, the new Tier 3 rotation (cycle 13, round 1: Reverion, Convion, Hexis, Doosan Fuel Cell, SK ecoplant, Watt Fuel Cell) and two further Tier 3 sweeps, and broad AI-datacenter/hyperscaler (English and German), regulation, competing-power, market/financials, research/IP and scientific-paper checks all returned only recycled/already-logged background (see notes below). Nothing confirmed beat or neared any row in SOFC_Benchmark_Records.md. For Dominic: no action needed on the LCOE model beyond the Ceres licensing note above; SPP's own FERC large-load show-cause answer (due Nov 20) still has not produced analyzable trade-press coverage, now seven days running, and the FERC Docket No. EL26-68 (Commissioner Lacerte's concurrence, Southwest Power Pool) item remains unfetched. items.text: Elcogen (priority): 25 days quiet (since the Nov 2 Hygreen Energy MoU). No new item found today in English or German sources; results recirculated the already-logged May 2026 elcoStack E3000 G2 mass-manufacturable platform launch and the Sept 2026 Metrosert testing-expansion deal.

Topsoe (priority): 92 days quiet on SOFC/SOEC specifically (since the Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset). No new item found today; Topsoe's press feed remains active but non-solid-oxide (SOEC-for-PtX, e-methanol with Forestal, e-SAF with Carbon Neutral Fuels, DKK 25M grid-access funding, DKK 4.4bn PtX restructuring) in both English and German searches.

Ceres Power (Tier 2, round 2 of current cycle): New item today — a sixth SOFC manufacturing licensee signed (unnamed, EMEA region, Endura platform, c. 200 MW/yr planned capacity); see Top Signals for full detail. This is a licensing/business-development update, not a technical KPI.
Sunfire (Tier 2, round 2 of current cycle): No new item; results recycled the standing Schwarzheide SOEC pilot-plant commissioning timeline (targeted end of 2026).

Tier 2 sweep ("Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra"): no new item; recycled Bloom's 2024-vintage 60% efficiency milestone and a dateless "Bloom Energy to supply Daroga Power" listing.

Today's Tier 3 dedicated rotation (new cycle 13, round 1: Reverion, Convion, Hexis, Doosan Fuel Cell, SK ecoplant, Watt Fuel Cell): no new item for any of the six; results recycled the already-logged Doosan/Reverion $76.7-78M SOFC stack-supply agreement, SK Ecoplant's 2021-2024 Korean heat-supply/localization background, and Watt Fuel Cell's residential WATT HOME rollout (non-data-center, non-SOFC-scale).

Tier 3 sweeps ("Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR Doosan Fuel Cell OR SK ecoplant"; "OxEon Energy OR Nexceris OR Kawasaki Heavy Industries OR Miura OR Weichai"): no new item for either; recycled the Miura/Ceres 4.2kW CHP launch and Weichai/Ceres manufacturing-licence/CE-certification background.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter, AEP/Google Cheyenne Fuel Cell LLC (702 MW/$4B, 20-yr PPA), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (28 MW, operational), NTT DATA (900 MW, global, shipments from 2027).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), Texas CRA (75 MW), SDCL (up to 450 MW). Also hosting the DOE/national-lab-backed StabilityMax R&D testbed in Danbury, CT. No named commercial deployment live yet.
Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B); supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment.

Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai, Denso, Thermax, + an unnamed new EMEA licensee signed Nov 16, 2026): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly, and the new EMEA licensee's remit is general EMEA-market manufacturing, not data-center-specific.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
EGEN Energy (China, watch-list): Pre-commercial/early-stage; no named data-center customer yet.
